conclusions: Base and small both fail the requested Punjabi Gurmukhi script on the original two clips.
Small lowers Urdu character-edit rates on these two clips and preserves the six word in the second, but still has recognition errors.
Small Punjabi clip1 deteriorates into unrelated mixed text; it is not an overall Urdu/Punjabi shipping recommendation.
No official Q4 file exists in the pinned upstream revision; no extra quantization model was downloaded.
Small exceeds the current180MiB app speech-file cap; direct JNI benchmarking bypassed that file guard.
limits: Published tiny timings came from the previous machine. One current tiny Punjabi control reproduces its transcript exactly, but this does not establish timing equivalence.
Current runs used shared4CPU/16GiB host, Release generic SIMD-off JNI, two threads per process, occasionally overlapping another approved two-thread experiment.
WER/CER use the same simple Unicode/punctuation recipe as the baseline. Cross-script Punjabi scores are not fluency measures.
The same two language clips are insufficient for broad claims; additional held-out cases are reserved until a candidate is shortlisted.
Small English controls were not run because the initial Punjabi script/content failures made it an unsuitable overall candidate.
